Coriantumr variant (new rule set beside Tyranny and standard), succession when a king is captured. CHOSEN, Derek's own answer to AskUserQuestion 2026-10-07: (1) If the king is captured and the queen is alive she takes on the king's ROLE with no change of piece or title ('she takes on the role of king without switching her piece or title. No one else gets promoted at that point'). (2) If the queen is captured nothing replaces her ('technically there is no need to promote someone else to queen'). (3) Ties between equally close pieces use a fixed rule, queenside first, no pop-up (the option marked Recommended). WHY: Derek frames it as 'about who is in command of the kingdom'; king and queen already move identically (both 4 squares any direction) so the queen needs no transformation. RULES OUT: (a) the chain-of-command reading where the closest bishop becomes a new queen when the queen steps up; (b) renaming or re-typing the queen; (c) an owner-picks pop-up for ties, for now. NOT SETTLED, asked next: what taking command changes for a bishop, knight or rook once no royal is left, and how a pawn becomes a king or queen ('Pawns are the only ones that can become a king or queen'). Do not build the succession code until those two are answered.

Coriantumr succession, FINAL model after Derek's second AskUserQuestion answers, 2026-10-07. CHOSEN BY DEREK (his option labels): when the line of succession reaches a bishop, knight or rook with no royal left, that piece 'It becomes a king' (up to 4 squares any direction, drawn as a king); a pawn becomes a king or queen by 'Far-rank promotion' (a king if only the queen is left, besides the usual Q/R/B/N). MY RECONCILIATION, NOT ASKED, FLAG FOR CONFIRMATION: my option text for the pawn question said 'Succession itself never changes a piece into a king', which contradicts his answer to the first question. I follow his ORIGINAL rule text ('If no rooks are on the board, then it moves to the pawns'): the line ends with pawns, so a pawn is crowned by succession too when no bishop, knight or rook remains. That is also what makes 'last man standing is the king' true for every ending. DERIVED RULE, equivalent to his queen-takes-the-role rule and needing no commander field on the board: after a capture, if a side still has pieces but no king piece and no queen, the closest bishop (else knight, else rook, else pawn) becomes a king. Closest = squared straight-line distance to the capture square; tie = lower file, then lower rank. Far-rank promotion adds KING as a choice only when the side has no king piece. Invariant: every non-empty side holds a king or a queen. RULES OUT: a commander/ruler flag in the state; a replacement queen; re-typing the queen; an owner-picks tie pop-up for now. STILL UNMEASURED: whether anyone can force the last capture against a lone 4-square king (retrograde analysis before any draw-rule decision).
